report:
Reviewed the complete production_execution claim, six ordinary implementation entries and four ordinary associated tests; no TODO or N/A entries exist. The production path is concrete: CompileTest::prepare materializes its source and generated manifest, calls SageHost::try_open, then observe::collect. Host metadata.rs uses Cargo metadata and the pinned sysroot; driver.rs registers source inputs, constructs the production Database and root module through parse_str_to_cst, and opens a separate rustc metadata stub containing extern declarations. parse/exprs.rs parses the fixture syntax without receiving expectations. observe.rs requests expanded_module_items, signatures and function.body, and obtains diagnostics and completed typed trees through those production queries. This is an assessment of harness routing, not a claim that every Rust language construct is supported. The inline API currently generates a dependency-free manifest, so its real external metadata is supplied by the pinned standard library; metadata.rs deliberately skips compiling this selected package in that case.

Expected types, diagnostic renderings and query logs never enter semantic queries: prepare inspects only whether expectation fields are present; collect receives markers and a query-capture boolean, derives observations from checked bodies and captures actual inspection events. run compares returned strings with expectations only after successful preparation. completed_types_ignore_expected_text_and_use_later_constraints runs identical sources with contradictory invented expectations and asserts identical u16 observations and no diagnostics. This visibly guards semantic independence; the same prepare/run boundary excludes both diagnostic and query expectation contents.

invalid_source_reaches_sage supplies a bool where u16 is required and asserts Sage's actual type-mismatch rendering and location. The metadata stub never contains that body, so rustc metadata initialization cannot reject it; the conformance run in compile/rustc.rs separately checks the actual fixture and does not substitute metadata-provider success for conformance. Its result is saved while Sage executes, preserving negative-fixture evaluation. The test's shared ERROR marker is checked independently by both compilers.

Setup errors propagate as Result errors before expected-source matching; unknown_edition_fails_setup asserts the direct unknown-edition error. Provider readiness uses a separate Result channel and rejects fatal/exited/failed expansion startup; failed_metadata_provider_replacement_preserves_the_live_host injects an invalid rustc option and asserts an actual metadata-provider error while the previous live host remains usable. It exercises the same try_open_with_args path used for initialization. CompileTest propagates this error with ? before observe::collect; it cannot be matched as a source diagnostic.

Ran cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests invalid_source_reaches_sage -- --exact (1 passed), cargo test -p sage-test-harness completed_types_ignore_expected_text_and_use_later_constraints (1 selected test passed), cargo test -p sage-test-harness unknown_edition_fails_setup (1 selected test passed), and cargo test -p sage-host failed_metadata_provider_replacement_preserves_the_live_host (1 passed; expected invalid-option stderr). Source inspection and these executions agree. Added associations for the existing three complementary tests and both essential harness execution helpers, then restarted review against those inputs. Captured the provider test fixture and review policy through review read. No behavioral edits or remaining requested edits.
